task_statement:
Research question (as posed on 2026-11-01, in the area of player absence and offensive reorganization):
The teammate with the closest pre-absence initiation profile (or most minutes / initiations / same-position minutes) is the largest gainer in the absent player's primary types.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): n=148; 148 spells; 11 cases

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

methodological_questions: How to define spells of absence.
How to measure pre-absence initiation profile similarity.
How to identify the absent player's primary play types.
How to quantify a teammate's gain in those play types after absence.
How to handle confounders like multiple concurrent absences, lineup changes, and opponent effects.
How to address small sample size and low base rates.
evidence_establishes: No prior studies were retrieved; nothing is established by the project's historical record.
evidence_does_not_establish: No prior evidence found; all aspects of the question remain open and unvalidated.
own_inferences: The question posits that similarity in pre-absence initiation profiles predicts which teammate will see the largest increase in the absent player's primary play types. This is a within-team, between-players comparison per absence spell.
The available data provide only 11 cases (likely absence spells meeting some selection criteria) and at most 148 spells overall. With so few independent units, any test will be severely underpowered.

Operationalizing 'closest pre-absence initiation profile' requires choosing a distance metric (e.g. cosine similarity, Euclidean distance on play-type share vectors) and an aggregation window. The reliability of these profiles is low for players with few initiations.
The definition of 'absent player's primary types' and 'largest gainer' needs precise quantitative thresholds; post-hoc definitions would inflate false-positive rates.
Confounding factors such as multiple concurrent injuries, coaching decisions, opponent strength, and regression to the mean cannot be adequately controlled with n=11.
uncertainties: The exact criteria for defining an absence spell (minimum games missed, exclusion of overlapping absences) were not specified.
The precise measure of initiation profile similarity was not specified (cosine, correlation, rank-order, etc.).

It is unclear whether 'largest gainer' refers to absolute increase in initiations, share of team initiations, or points produced, and whether it is measured within the same spell window or compared to a baseline expectation.
The number 11 cases may refer to a specific subset (e.g., absences of players above a usage threshold) and the true sample size might be slightly different, but remains very small.

historical_effect.explanation: The retrieval returned zero records; no previous studies informed the decision.

blocking_constraints.text: Only 11 cases (or 148 total spells) are available, which is far too few for a between-players comparison within each absence spell while controlling for confounders. Power to detect a non-zero predictive relationship is near zero.
Many teammates will have very few pre-absence initiations in the relevant play types, making similarity estimates unreliable and prone to spurious extremeness.

Selecting the 'closest' teammate by similarity in pre-absence data may pick players with spuriously high similarity due to random noise; their subsequent gain would be subject to regression to the mean, creating an illusory effect.

prior_work.summary: No prior study family was returned by the retrieval tool; prior work on this exact question is unknown.

risks.text: With only 11 independent cases, any statistical test will lack power to detect even large effects, making null and alternative outcomes indistinguishable from noise.
Play-type initiation vectors are sparse; many teammates lack enough possessions to form a reliable profile, leading to unstable similarity rankings.
Choosing the teammate with the closest pre-absence profile selects for a noisy extreme; gains measured afterward may reflect regression to the mean rather than a causal effect.
Initiation-profile similarity metrics have not been validated for this use case; measurement error will attenuate or inflate relationships unpredictably.
Defining the absent player's 'primary types' from the same pre-absence data and then measuring gain in those types can create circularity and overfitting.
Concurrent injuries, lineup changes, opponent strength, schedule density, and coaching decisions all affect who gains initiations and are not accounted for.
If the absent player's primary play types are infrequent overall, even large relative increases in initiations will consist of few possessions, making the signal highly variable.
Multiple teammates per spell are compared; failing to adjust for the implicit selection of the 'largest gainer' will inflate the false-positive rate.

design.estimand: For each qualified absence spell, the within-team rank-order correlation between (a) the similarity of each teammate's pre-absence initiation profile to the absent player's profile and (b) the change in that teammate's share of team initiations in the absent player's two primary play types (post-absence minus pre-absence). The null hypothesis is that this correlation is zero.
design.unit: One qualified absence spell (a continuous series of games missed by one player, minimum 5 games, with no other player missing more than 2 games in the same span).
design.sample: All absence spells from the available seasons (2022-23 through 2025-26) meeting the unit criteria and having at least 7 available teammates with ≥ 30 pre-absence initiations. Expected available spells after filtering: insufficient (likely < 15, too few for a reliable aggregate test).
design.power: A simulation-based power analysis assuming a true rank correlation of 0.3 per spell, 20 spells, and a one-sample t-test on Fisher-z-transformed correlations would require approximately 30 spells for 80 % power at α=0.05. The actual maximum possible spells (11–148) is too small and would yield power below 30 %.
design.controls: Number of concurrent injuries, team strength (pre-absence net rating), opponent strength (rolling 10-game opponent defensive rating), home/away share, and whether the absent player is a primary initiator (usage > 20 %). However, with the small sample these cannot be reliably included.
design.falsification: Placebo test: repeat the analysis using randomly chosen ‘absent’ player spells from games they actually played, expecting no consistent correlation; also check that the correlation for the most-similar teammate is no larger than for the teammate with median similarity.
design.multiplicity: Only one test statistic (the mean or median within-spell rank correlation). No multiple comparisons across play types or thresholds.
design.decision_rule: Reject the null if the meta-analytic mean of the within-spell rank correlations exceeds 0 with a one-sided p < 0.05 (random-effects meta-analysis). Non-parametric bootstrap of spells will confirm robustness.
design.data_version: Per-game play-by-play and derived play-type possession records as of 2026-11-01, NBA seasons 2022-23 through 2025-26.
